description_full: Moncler S.p.A., together with its subsidiaries, engages in the production and distribution of garments, children's clothing, footwear, eyewear and other related accessories under the Moncler and Stone Island brands. It also provides leather goods; bags, backpacks, and accessories; and glasses. The company operates through directly operated stores, e-concessions, multi-brand sales outlets, shop-in-shops in luxury department stores, airport locations, and online luxury multi-brand retailers. It also sells its products through moncler.com, an online store. It operates in Italy, rest of Europe, Asia, the Middle East, Africa, and the United States. Moncler S.p.A. was founded in 1952 and is headquartered in Milan, Italy.
culture_narrative: Employs approximately 8K people. Revenue per employee of $428K ranks in the above the sector median among Consumer Cyclical peers. Each employee generates $101K of free cash flow annually. Stock-based compensation of $5K per employee reflects an ownership culture. Governance score flags low compensation governance risk (2/10).
financial_summary: Moncler S.P.A. is a large-cap consumer cyclical business with a $12.5B market cap on $3.4B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +9% over the past three years, a respectable pace for a business of this size.
Returns on capital run at 22% against a 8% cost of capital — a 14-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat. Gross margins of 78% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $813M in free cash flow — roughly 24 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.53× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage of 21× is fortress-like.

Shareholder yield of 3.1% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insiders hold 18% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and within its sector the business captures 3.7× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.

sect: Its 29% operating margin runs 22pp above the Consumer Cyclical median (8%), a real cost or pricing edge over peers.
It captures 3.66x its revenue share in sector profits, taking a disproportionate slice of the profit pool.
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.03 across 380 companies in the universe; the top four hold 25% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares are in a steep downtrend, down 23% over the past year excluding the latest month.
The price sits near the bottom of its 52-week range, 34% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 46% and a beta of 0.66, it is more defensive than the market.
Trading is thin (about $25K a day), below the $1.0M liquidity floor flagged; building a position would move the price.
In past sell-offs it fell 40% in the 2020 crash and 46% in the 2022 bear market.
val: The stock trades only 10% below its DCF fair value of $51.33, a thin margin of safety.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 34%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $39.54 to $68.68 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
On multiples it looks expensive against Consumer Cyclical peers: EV/EBITDA 13.9 vs 10.5 (sector median).
Earnings yields are mixed: an FCF yield of 6.5% (above the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 7.9% (vs the 8% bar).
The price implies 0.2% annual cash-flow growth, 8pp less than the model expects.
prof: ROIC of 22% clears the cost of capital of 8.0% by 14pp, the mark of a value creator; returns have been steady (CV 0.04).
It runs a 78% gross margin and converts 24% of revenue into free cash flow.
Earnings quality looks solid: cash conversion of 1.53x.
ROE of 16% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (1.5x equity multiplier).
hlth: The balance sheet carries net cash of $365.3M.
No distress or manipulation flags (Altman Z 4.7, in the safe zone).
growth: Revenue has compounded at 8.9% over 3 years.
At current returns, reinvesting 35% of profits supports about 7.7% a year of fundamental growth, enough to sustain growth.
own: Insiders own 18.2%, meaningful skin in the game, and institutions hold 55%.
It returns 3.1% a year to shareholders (3.5% in dividends).
people: With about 8,032 employees, each generates about $428K of revenue, in line with the Consumer Cyclical median.
That works out to $101K of free cash flow per employee.
Compensation governance scores well (2/10, lower is better).
